19.old: Route 722 (Bonson / Meadowtown) is a loop that uses Harris Road, Ford Road, 190A Street, Hammond Road, Blakely Road, 116B Avenue and Bonson Road to reach Fraser Way and the Barnston View roundabout. Pitt Meadows Station is one of its stops
19.new: Route 722 (Bonson / Meadowtown) is a loop. It goes along Harris Road, Ford Road and 190A Street, then Hammond Road and Blakely Road, 116B Avenue and Bonson Road, ending at Fraser Way and the Barnston View roundabout. One of its stops is Pitt Meadows Station.

21.old: Route 719 (Fraser Way / Meadowtown) continues from the 722 and uses Fraser Way, Bonson Road, Wildwood and Hammond Road before it reaches Maple Meadows Station in Maple Ridge
21.new: Route 719 (Fraser Way / Meadowtown) picks up where the 722 leaves off. It runs on Wildwood, Hammond Road, Bonson Road and Fraser Way, then arrives at Maple Meadows Station in Maple Ridge.

43.old: Pitt Meadows is in School District 42 (SD42). Names, grades and addresses from the Province’s SD42 school list and each school’s website. Checked against the official pages on October 18, 2026.
43.new: Pitt Meadows belongs to School District 42 (SD42). Each school’s website and the Province’s list for SD42 supply the names, grades and addresses, which were compared with the official pages as of October 18, 2026.

100.old: The City says it is moving forward with planned expansion of the park to help create a centralized community “sports hub”
100.new: To help build a centralized community “sports hub”, the City says it is moving ahead with the planned expansion of the park.

119.old: The City’s Official Community Plan, adopted September 27, 2022, describes Goal 5 as a walkable and compact community that offers easy access to nature and amenities, with a range of housing options
119.new: Goal 5 of the Official Community Plan, which the City adopted on September 27, 2022, is a walkable, compact community with easy access to nature and amenities and a range of housing options.

125.old: Lot size (MLS sales data, not an official source): the median lot size of detached houses sold between July 1 and October 8, 2026 was 7,204 sq ft, based on 10 sales with a recorded lot size.
125.new: MLS sales data is not an official source, but it puts the median lot size for detached houses that sold from July 1 to October 8, 2026 at 7,204 sq ft, from 10 sales where a lot size was recorded.

143.old: The City adopted its Official Community Plan, “I See Pitt Meadows 2040”, on September 27, 2022. Goal 2 is a community where agriculture is the dominant land use and farmland is protected for food production. Goal 5 is a walkable and compact community with a range of housing options.
143.new: On September 27, 2022 the City adopted “I See Pitt Meadows 2040” as its Official Community Plan. Goal 2 is about farmland being protected for food production, with agriculture as the dominant use of land. Goal 5 calls for a compact, walkable community and a range of housing options.

145.old: The Pitt Meadows / Maple Ridge Diking District covers 3,546 hectares (3,136 in Pitt Meadows). The City says the urban development area is drainage Area 3 (Kennedy, including McKechnie), served by ditches, culverts and storm sewers, and that low-lying catchments drain to the Pitt, Alouette and Fraser Rivers through floodboxes and pump stations.
145.new: The Pitt Meadows / Maple Ridge Diking District takes in 3,546 hectares, 3,136 of them in Pitt Meadows. The City identifies drainage Area 3 (Kennedy, including McKechnie) as the urban development area, served by ditches, culverts and storm sewers. Low-lying catchments empty into the Pitt, Alouette and Fraser Rivers by way of floodboxes and pump stations.

146.old: The City says it is almost entirely protected by 60 km of dikes, which protect the City’s low-lying areas and key infrastructure from river flooding.
146.new: The City says that it is almost completely protected by 60 km of dikes, which keep river flooding away from low-lying areas and key infrastructure.

148.old: The City’s Financial Plan 2026–2030 says over 85% of Pitt Meadows’ land base lies within the floodplains of the Fraser, Pitt and Alouette rivers.
148.new: Per the City’s Financial Plan 2026–2030, more than 85% of the land base in Pitt Meadows is within the Fraser, Pitt and Alouette rivers’ floodplains.

149.old: The City’s Financial Plan 2026–2030 says agriculture remains the predominant land use in Pitt Meadows and that 78% of Pitt Meadows land falls within the Agricultural Land Reserve.
149.new: The Financial Plan 2026–2030 from the City describes land use in Pitt Meadows as still predominantly agricultural, with 78% of the land inside the Agricultural Land Reserve.

151.old: The City says Pitt Meadows has one West Coast Express station, Pitt Meadows Station, in the urban core. It is on Harris Road, which is in my Central Meadows guide area, not in South Meadows.
151.new: According to the City, Pitt Meadows Station, located in the urban core, is the only West Coast Express station in Pitt Meadows. It sits on Harris Road, and that road falls in my Central Meadows guide area rather than South Meadows.

152.old: Route 595 (Langley Centre / Maple Meadows Station) does not enter Pitt Meadows: it runs between Langley Centre and Maple Meadows Station in Maple Ridge.
152.new: Route 595 (Langley Centre / Maple Meadows Station) never enters Pitt Meadows. It connects Langley Centre with Maple Meadows Station, which is in Maple Ridge.

156.old: Ask the City what the dikes, drainage and floodplain mapping mean for the exact address, especially for a basement or an addition.
156.new: Check with the City on how the dikes, drainage and floodplain mapping affect the specific address, particularly where a basement or an addition is involved.

158.old: Ask the City what the Official Community Plan designations allow on the lots around the home, because new buildings can change a street.
158.new: Because new buildings can change a street, check with the City about what the Official Community Plan designations permit on the neighbouring lots.

182.old: Route 722 (Bonson / Meadowtown) is a loop that uses Harris Road, Ford Road, 190A Street, Hammond Road, Blakely Road, 116B Avenue and Bonson Road to reach Fraser Way and the Barnston View roundabout. Pitt Meadows Station is one of its stops.
182.new: Pitt Meadows Station is a stop on Route 722 (Bonson / Meadowtown), a loop made up of Bonson Road, 116B Avenue, Blakely Road and Hammond Road, together with Harris Road, Ford Road and 190A Street, that connects to Fraser Way and the Barnston View roundabout.

183.old: Route 719 (Fraser Way / Meadowtown) continues from the 722 and uses Fraser Way, Bonson Road, Wildwood and Hammond Road before it reaches Maple Meadows Station in Maple Ridge.
183.new: After the 722, Route 719 (Fraser Way / Meadowtown) carries on via Fraser Way and Bonson Road, then Wildwood and Hammond Road, finishing at Maple Meadows Station in Maple Ridge.

184.new: Timetable dates: the 722 and 719 routes took effect September 7, 2026, according to TransLink’s timetable PDFs, which I read on October 18, 2026. Check the current timetable.

185.old: The City says Pitt Meadows has one West Coast Express station, Pitt Meadows Station, in the urban core. It is on Harris Road, which is in my Central Meadows guide area, not in South Meadows.
185.new: Pitt Meadows has a single West Coast Express station, Pitt Meadows Station, and the City places it in the urban core. The station is on Harris Road, which belongs to my Central Meadows guide area and not to South Meadows.

188.old: Pitt Meadows Secondary (Grades 8 to 12, 19438 116B Avenue) is the only public secondary school in Pitt Meadows on the Province’s SD42 list. The Province says a new school on the same property is expected to open for students by fall 2029.
188.new: Pitt Meadows Secondary, at 19438 116B Avenue, serves Grades 8 to 12. It is the sole public secondary school in Pitt Meadows according to the Province’s SD42 list, and the Province says that a new school on that same property should open to students by fall 2029.

192.old: The Pitt Meadows Public Library is at 200 – 12099 Harris Road, in the civic centre near City Hall and the Family Recreation Centre. I found no other library branch in Pitt Meadows.
192.new: You’ll find the Pitt Meadows Public Library at 200 – 12099 Harris Road, within the civic centre close to City Hall and the Family Recreation Centre. Pitt Meadows has no other library branch that I could find.

194.old: The City adopted its Official Community Plan, “I See Pitt Meadows 2040”, on September 27, 2022. Goal 2 is a community where agriculture is the dominant land use and farmland is protected for food production. Goal 5 is a walkable and compact community with a range of housing options.
194.new: “I See Pitt Meadows 2040” is the Official Community Plan the City adopted on September 27, 2022. Goal 2 envisions agriculture as the dominant land use, with farmland safeguarded for growing food. Goal 5 envisions a compact and walkable community offering a range of housing options.

197.old: The Pitt Meadows / Maple Ridge Diking District covers 3,546 hectares (3,136 in Pitt Meadows). The City says the urban development area is drainage Area 3 (Kennedy, including McKechnie), served by ditches, culverts and storm sewers, and that low-lying catchments drain to the Pitt, Alouette and Fraser Rivers through floodboxes and pump stations.
197.new: The Diking District for Pitt Meadows and Maple Ridge covers 3,546 hectares, of which 3,136 lie in Pitt Meadows.
